question:
An engineer must implement access control for Cisco UCS Manager. The configuration must meet these requirements:
- All users and user groups must be configured using Active Directory.
- User1 must have full access to the Fabric Interconnect infrastructure and network security operations.
- User1 must have full access to the storage operations configuration.
Which action must be performed on Cisco UCS to meet the requirements?
options: Execute a built-in role for the user and RADIUS for the role-mapping for Active Directory.
Execute a built-in role for the user and LDAP for the role-mapping for Active Directory.
Create a custom role for the user and LDAP for the role-mapping for Active Directory.
Create a custom role for the user and RADIUS for the role-mapping for Active Directory.
theory: Because User1 needs a nonstandard combination of privileges - full Network Administrator scope (fabric interconnect and network security) plus full Storage Administrator scope together - no single built-in UCS role covers exactly that combination, so a custom role combining both privilege sets must be created. Since the organization authenticates through Active Directory, LDAP group mapping (rather than RADIUS, which needs per-user AV-pair attributes instead of group-based mapping) is used to tie AD groups directly to that custom role for role assignment. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 19 - LDAP Group Mapping, custom roles)
